headline: Avecho Biotechnology CEO highlights phase three interim analysis success for CBD insomnia product, describing it as a major de-risking event ahead of TGA registration
reasoning: Avecho's enhanced cannabidiol product targeting insomnia has passed its interim analysis in a pivotal phase three clinical trial, allowing the trial to continue to completion. CEO Paul Gavin says if the second cohort behaves like the first, the trial will be statistically significant and support a TGA registration application. The company already has Sandoz — the world's largest pharmaceutical generics company — as its commercial partner for Australia. Gavin notes the company has approximately $6.5 million in the bank, does not need to raise capital immediately, and plans to fund trial completion through licensing deals for additional territories. He characterises the company as the cheapest ASX company in a phase three clinical trial and the product as significantly de-risked following the interim analysis. The Australian market alone has 9.5 million insomniacs, with additional demand expected from pain, anxiety and menopause patients; global expansion including FDA discussions is planned for the second half of 2025.
quote: So I mean, the interim analysis was the key risk. It was pun intended. It was what kept us up at night. So this was the first big, uh, proof that the product that we have developed has, um, action or efficacy against the target indication, which was insomnia. The rest of the trial is much more procedural. Um, so everyone does acknowledge that it is a significant de-risking event. It doesn't just de-risk the product, de-risk the trial, and it de-risk the company. So it's a much better investment thesis moving forward.
episode_title: Avecho looks to put insomnia to bed
